requirement:
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.

Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`. I did not request implementation source, because the test inputs and assertions were enough to judge.

**1. A function with no attributable execution needs an accepted exception, even when its file meets the threshold.**
- `overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent` has a one-line file with 1/1 line executed. The check still fails with `#fn[outer]: zero execution`.
- `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` expects `#trait[T]/fn[body]: zero execution` and `#fn[excluded]: not measured`.
- `methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported` expects `zero execution` for a method, a test and a helper.
- `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` shows two things. A file-level exception does not waive the function, so the check still fails with `#fn[a]: zero execution`. A function-level accepted citation makes the check pass, and the exception is listed as `code.rs#fn[a]: zero execution`.
- The same test also covers the other branches. An unmeasured function passes when the accepted citation covers it. The check passes when the function is executed and no exception is needed. It fails when the review determination is false. It reports an error when the review is a `{fixme}`.
- The positive case, where an executed function passes, is also covered by the `covered` record and by `full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests`.

**2. Execution attributable only to a nested function or closure must not cover the enclosing function.**
- `overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent` has a closure and an inner function with counts, and `outer` is still reported zero. The second run reverses this: outer executed and inner zero. It asserts `#fn[outer]/fn[inner]: zero execution` and that `#fn[outer]:` is not reported.
- `expanded_async_entries_match_the_fn_keyword_without_borrowing_closure_execution` shows the first run passing when the counter sits at the `fn` keyword after `async`. The second run, with only the closure counter present, fails with `#fn[work]: not measured`.
- The real-flow test `full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests` uses real counters. It asserts `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution` and that `#fn[outer]: zero execution` is absent.

**3. Having no recorded lines alone must not establish that there are no obligations.**
- `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` checks three cases.
  - A file with only a struct and a bodiless trait declaration is reported `no executable obligations — pass`.
  - A file with `fn missing() {}` and no recorded lines is reported `code.rs: not measured — FAIL`, with `#fn[missing]: not measured`.
  - A file that fails to parse makes the check fail.
- `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` adds inventory assertions. A bodiless declaration alone counts as no obligation, but a macro call or a derive attribute is not treated as proof of none.

**Delegated obligations.** The exception-invalidation and portability rules belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Scope and discovery failures belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`, and the test `methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported` also covers discovery failure. The 80% file threshold belongs to `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`. This requirement does not need separate tests for them.

All the tests listed above carry `{test}` references to the subject.

Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
